title: Add built‑in graceful shutdown handling for HTTP server
description: Ensures the framework can safely terminate on SIGINT/SIGTERM by stopping new connections, waiting for in‑flight requests, and releasing resources. This improves production stability and prevents data loss during deployments or container restarts.
testCases: When SIGTERM is sent, the server stops accepting new requests within the configured timeout.
Pending requests are allowed to finish before the server fully closes.
acceptance: Calling `app.enableGracefulShutdown({ timeout: 5000 })` registers signal handlers. After `app.listen`, sending SIGTERM triggers a shutdown sequence: no new connections are accepted, existing connections are given up to 5 s to finish, then the process exits with code 0. The promise returned by `enableGracefulShutdown` resolves only after the server is fully closed.
reason: Production environments require clean termination to avoid abrupt request aborts, resource leaks, and inconsistent state, making this a critical feature for any deployment pipeline.
